extracted.intended_audience: Harvard Faculty (FAS) and research administrators seeking funding and proposal-development support
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for FAS faculty and research administrators to discover, prioritize, and prepare applications for internal and external research funding, including use of databases, internal limited-submission processes, and proposal-development support.

rubrics_metrics.name: FORA Research Development support
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Development (RD) team in the FAS Office of Research Administration (FORA) offers a range of resources to help researchers identify funding opportunities and is available to work individually with FAS faculty and administrators to strategize and identify suitable funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RD provides guidance on using searchable grant databases, curated lists by discipline, focused funding sources (internal programs, limited submissions, early career awards, sabbatical fellowships), individual consultations, recommendations for programs aligned with faculty needs, and tailored funding alerts using commercial databases available to Harvard affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: FORA-managed grants administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Development manages the application and review process for three internal funding programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FORA is the gateway for these internal programs and handles internal administration and review for the Dean’s Competitive Fund for Promising Scholarship, Star‑Friedman Challenge for Promising Scientific Research, and the Zuckerman Travel and Research STEM Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dean’s Competitive Fund funding categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dean’s Competitive Fund for Promising Scholarship is a targeted program that provides funding in the categories Bridge Funding, Seed Funding, and Enabling Infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align requests to one of these three categories (bridge, seed, enabling infrastructure) when seeking Dean’s Competitive Fund support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star‑Friedman Challenge scope and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Star‑Friedman Challenge for Promising Scientific Research offers opportunities for eligible faculty to seek support for new work in their research programs within the life, physical, and social sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should propose new work within those disciplinary areas and applicants should confirm eligibility as defined by the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zuckerman Travel and Research STEM Fund purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zuckerman Travel and Research STEM Fund aims to support the development of new research collaborations in STEM fields between faculty members and their counterparts at research institutions in Israel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project designs should clearly focus on initiating or developing collaborative research ties with Israeli research institutions; travel and collaborative activities are central to the fund’s purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvard internal funding across career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Harvard Funding: grant programs and award opportunities from within Harvard support FAS faculty at every career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should explore internal Harvard programs tailored to different career stages and roles; RD curates listings for these internal opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early career award eligibility windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Early Career: opportunities targeted to encourage professional success for faculty who are building their independent research careers, generally with eligibility defined by a certain timeframe post‑PhD or within a certain timeframe after starting a faculty appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must verify the specific temporal eligibility window (years since PhD or since appointment) for each early‑career program and align their application accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited submission compliance and internal selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited Submission Opportunities: sponsors restrict the number of applications accepted from Harvard; eligible applications are managed through an internal process to select the most competitive proposal(s) to represent the university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sponsor limits submissions, faculty must participate in the university’s internal selection process; plan ahead for internal deadlines and selection criteria used to nominate campus candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbatical funding characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sabbatical Opportunities: primarily long‑term opportunities during which fellows are immersed in their scholarship and an in‑person community, available at a variety of locations worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should reflect sustained, immersive scholarly plans and community engagement appropriate to sabbatical fellowships and conform to host site expectations and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral funding purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral Scholars Opportunities: support options available to postdoctoral researchers; postdoctoral research grants offer stipend support to advance research or assist with transitioning to research independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoc proposals should articulate how stipend support will advance research training or transition the scholar toward independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external funding databases
rubrics_metrics.description: External Funding Databases: Pivot, Foundation Directory Online (FDO), Grants.gov, and SPIN are recommended resources to search for funding opportunities from a variety of sponsors worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pivot aggregates global grants/fellowships/prizes; FDO provides sponsor profiles and data to match sponsor goals to research; Grants.gov lists open U.S. federal funding opportunities and provides guidance on grant policies; SPIN (Harvard subscription) covers domestic and global opportunities. Use these databases to identify appropriate sponsors and tailor searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal competitiveness and responsiveness to funder criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Resources: FORA has compiled information and resources to help enhance proposal competitiveness and offers grantsmanship advice, successful sample proposals, and feedback on a proposal draft’s responsiveness to the funder’s review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use sample proposals, seek RD grantsmanship feedback, and explicitly demonstrate responsiveness to the funder’s stated review criteria in their application narratives and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow proposal submission timeline and onboarding resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Process Overview: view the proposal submission timeline which provides an overview of the typical steps necessary for the preparation and submission of a proposal to an external sponsor; access proposal FAQs and onboarding resources for new faculty and research administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to typical preparation/submission steps and institutional timelines, consult FAQs for common procedural questions, and use onboarding materials if new to sponsored projects administration.
